extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, astronomers, and medical naturalists (readers/authors of the Philosophical Transactions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for compiling a comprehensive natural history of a subject (exemplified by Boyle's 'natural history of human blood'): how to organize material into hierarchical titles, classify experiments under those titles, and report observational data (astronomical and medical).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for compiling a natural history (overall organization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever occurs concerning the subject to be treated of, may be ranked under several orders or classes, agreeing in the general names of titles: the first or primary order ... to consist of such titles as shall comprehend the whole matter of the subject, as it appears at first view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the matter of any primary title increases, divide it according to its own nature into several subordinate branches, or secondary titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a mantissa (paralipomena and addenda)
rubrics_metrics.description: It will be useful that a mantissa should be subjoined to the first edition of the titles, consisting of paralipomena and addenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add a mantissa to the first edition of titles to capture omissions, addenda, and supplementary material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify experiments under primary titles
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2d part contains miscellaneous experiments and observations, about human blood, referable to some one of the titles of the first order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange experiments and observations so each is referable to an existing primary title; this ensures experiments are organized within the established hierarchical scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a dedicated part summarizing the topic and its relations
rubrics_metrics.description: The 4th part contains the history of the spirit of human blood begun; and is a summary of the history of volatile salts in general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a synthetic/historical summary section that situates the specific topic (e.g., spirit of blood) within broader related subjects (e.g., volatile salts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Document methods and outcomes in appendices (e.g., distillation procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the appendix, under the title of the several ways of distilling human blood, the author gives an account of his success in distilling three portions of dried blood, each with a different additament, as with quicklime, calcined tartar, and oil of vitriol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include technical appendix material describing experimental procedures, variations (different additives), and results to support reproducibility and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record daily observations and appearances for comet reports
rubrics_metrics.description: After noting the daily observations and appearances of the comet, tracing its course among the fixed stars, M. Hevelius from these deduces the following table of its motions and observed places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep a day-by-day observational log of positions and visual appearances as the basis for deducing motion tables and positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace a comet's course among fixed stars
rubrics_metrics.description: Tracing its course among the fixed stars ... deduces a table of its motions and observed places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate comet positions to nearby fixed stars to create an accurate path and generate a table of observed places and motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tabulate motions and observed places (quantitative reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: From daily observations and tracing among the stars, deduce a table of its motions and observed places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce explicit tabular data (dates, longitudes, latitudes, declination, right ascension, diurnal motion, etc.) to communicate the object's quantitative motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report whether comet motion is prograde or retrograde and quantify degrees
rubrics_metrics.description: Hence it appears that this comet moved retrograde, or contrary to the order of the signs, its motion in the ecliptic, during the interval in the table, being 63° 53', but 74° 35' in its own orbit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State direction of orbital motion (prograde/retrograde) and give measured angular motion both in the ecliptic and in the comet's orbit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report orbital inclinations to ecliptic and equinoctial
rubrics_metrics.description: Which was inclined to the ecliptic in an angle of 39°, but to the equinoctial 56°.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give inclinations relative to the ecliptic and equinoctial to describe orbital geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify latitude variation (north/south) over observation interval
rubrics_metrics.description: Its latitude at first was 29° 15' N. and at last 11° 20' S.; so that it varied its latitude almost 41°.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the comet's latitudinal positions over time with numeric values and compute total variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe the comet's head (diameter, brightness, nucleus presence, change over time)
rubrics_metrics.description: As to the head of this comet, its diameter at first was much less than afterwards; but, on the other hand, it was much brighter at first than towards the end. It exhibited no distinct and fulgent nucleus, ... but appeared a confused mass of matter, which became much thinner towards the conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterize head size, brightness evolution, presence/absence and distinctness of a nucleus, and textural changes through the apparition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe tail presence and classify comet type
rubrics_metrics.description: As it was seen mostly without a tail, it may be numbered among the hairy comets, or those that have beards like goats; for it extended upwards its very short and diluted bristles only till Aug. 18; which afterwards quite disappeared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note presence/absence of a tail, its length and texture (e.g., 'bristles'), temporal changes, and classify the comet (e.g., 'hairy').

rubrics_metrics.name: Note geometry and visibility of satellite ingress/emerison relative to Sun/opposition angles
rubrics_metrics.description: As the sun removes from the ... the ingresses of the satellites into his shadow become observable. When he is about 30° from it, the emersions of the 4th, and at 60°, of the 3d, begin to be seen between the shadow and body; continuing so till ... when the emersions of the 3d fall behind his body, but the emersions of the 4th continue visible till he be less than 30° distant ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting satellite occultations/immersions, provide the angular separations from the Sun/opposition at which ingresses and emersions become or cease to be observable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for optical instrument inversion effects on apparent orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: All the appearances being made really to the right hand ... though with inverting telescopes they appear the contrary, to the left.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether an inverting telescope was used and note that inversion reverses apparent left/right in recorded observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether blood may be ordered by fermentation or putrefaction to give a spirit (distillation sequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether human blood may be so ordered by fermentation or putrefaction, as that in distillation, a spirit, either urinous, or vinous, may ascend before the phlegm?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate and report whether specific preparatory processes (fermentation/putrefaction) yield a distilled spirit that precedes heavier residues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether 'spirit of human blood' is simply volatile salt mixed with phlegm
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether spirit of human blood be really any thing, but the volatile salt and phlegm well commixed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine constituent hypothesis: test whether the so-called spirit is merely a mixture of volatile salts and phlegm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine species of saline bodies to which spirit of blood is to be referred
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the species of saline bodies to which the spirit of human blood is to be referred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify the spirit among known saline species based on chemical/physical properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare spirit of blood with spirit of urine and other volatile alkalies
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether spirit of human blood be different from spirit of urine, and other spirits that are called volatile alkalies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform comparative analyses to establish similarities or differences with other volatile bodily spirits and alkalies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify the quantity of spirit contained in human blood (with/without serum, dried)
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the quantity of spirit contained in human blood, whether accompanied with its serum, or dried.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure the amount of spirit extractable from fresh (with serum) and dried blood samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report consistence and specific gravity of the spirit of blood
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the consistence and specific gravity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterize rheological properties and specific gravity of the spirit for identification and comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe odour, taste, colour, and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the odour, taste, colour, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sensory and optical descriptions (odour, taste where safe and appropriate, colour, transparency) as part of the natural history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess dissolutive power of spirit of human blood
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the dissolutive power of spirit of human blood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test the ability of the spirit to dissolve substances; report methods and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine tinctures that may be drawn with the spirit of human blood
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the tinctures that may be drawn with spirit of human blood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiment to extract tinctures using the spirit and report which dyes/tinctures it produces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report coagulating power
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the coagulating power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate and quantify the spirit's effect on coagulation processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report precipitating power
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the precipitating power of spirit of human blood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test precipitation reactions with various reagents and document outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate affinity between spirit of blood and some chemical oils and vinous spirits
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the affinity between spirit of human blood and some chemical oils, and vinous spirits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study interactions/affinities with oils and wine spirits to understand chemical behavior and compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report relation between spirit of human blood and the air
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the relation between spirit of human blood and the air.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine volatility, reactivity, or changes upon exposure to air; include observations on stability/oxidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess hostility of the spirit of human blood to acids (liquid and fumes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the hostility of the spirit of human blood to acids, whether they be in the form of liquors or fumes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test reactions with acids in various forms and document corrosive or decompositional effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe medicinal virtues of the spirit of human blood (external and internal application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the medicinal virtues of the spirit of human blood applied outwardly, and inwardly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate therapeutic effects (if any) when applied topically or internally, reporting methods, doses, and observed benefits or harms.
